items.stem: What is the primary aim of systems engineering on a large defense program?

options.text: To ensure the whole system meets stakeholder needs through disciplined requirements, integration and verification
options.rationale: Correct: systems engineering integrates parts into a validated whole.

options.text: To design a single component in isolation
options.rationale: Systems engineering spans the whole system, not one part.

options.text: To avoid ever testing the system
options.rationale: Verification and testing are central to systems engineering.

options.text: To skip stakeholder input to move faster
options.rationale: Stakeholder needs drive the whole process.

items.explanation: Correct: systems engineering integrates parts into a validated whole.

items.stem: Which TWO activities distinguish verification from validation? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Verification checks the system was built to its requirements
Validation checks the system meets the stakeholders' real needs
options.rationale: Correct: validation is 'built the right thing'.
Verification is based on the requirements.

items.stem: Why is interface management planned early in a complex program?

options.text: Interfaces between subsystems are a common source of integration risk
options.rationale: Correct: early interface control reduces costly late surprises.

options.text: Because interfaces never cause any problems
options.rationale: Interfaces are a leading integration risk.

options.text: Because it lets teams ignore requirements
options.rationale: Interface management supports, not replaces, requirements.
Integration is essential for complex systems.

items.explanation: Correct: early interface control reduces costly late surprises.
